walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit 2: The Study of Poetry 1900-Present and Drama 1900-Present — a core area of A-Level English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit 2: The Study of Poetry 1900-Present and Drama 1900-Present brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit 2: The Study of Poetry 1900-Present and Drama 1900-Present.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.

mcqs.q: What did Romantic poets value in nature?
options: Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Romantic poets just liked to write about pretty landscapes.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.
Nature as a source of spiritual insight and emotional truth, accessed through imagination — not picturesque scenery for its own sake.
Experimentation with form (fragmentation, stream of consciousness), focus on subjective interior experience, scepticism toward traditional narrative and absolute truth.
Modernism is literature about modern technology like phones.
Modernism just means literature written in modern times.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
